title: Case study: URL shortener
summary: Read-heavy key-value design run through the 45-minute framework: unique codes without coordination, a redirect hot path that survives viral links and cache restarts, an async analytics and abuse pipeline.

units.title: Guided design: requirements, estimation, API and model, HLD, three deep dives

labs.title: Unique short codes: base 62, keyed permutation, counter ranges with compare-and-swap, random codes with insert-if-absent

outcomes.text: Scope a shortener prompt in ≤ 6 minutes: core operations, NFRs with numbers, out-of-scope list, and the four clarifying questions (guessability, analytics, aliases, takedown SLA) whose answers change the architecture.
Estimate peak creates, peak redirects, storage with replication, the base-62 code length and its headroom, cache memory for the hot set and egress, and state which decision each number drives.

Design the API (idempotent create, a browser-followable 302 redirect with explicit caching semantics, 404 vs 410) and a data model whose partition key follows the dominant access pattern, and defend the store choice with a flip condition.
Draw a minimal, justified high-level design with both paths traced and rates on the arrows, and say what each box does when it fails.

Choose an ID scheme (random codes with insert-if-absent vs counter ranges with a keyed permutation vs a global counter vs URL hashing vs a key pool) using collision arithmetic, coordination cost, crash behaviour and guessability.

Implement base-62 codes, a bijective mixer, compare-and-swap range allocation with a per-node generator, and random codes with atomic insert-if-absent, and show with a break-it what a non-atomic counter does (labs/c1/keygen).

Design the redirect hot path: in-process L1 with request coalescing for a viral key, negative caching against enumeration, lazy expiry, a measurable takedown fan-out, and fail-open behaviour on a store outage.

Design the click-analytics pipeline (async events, durable log, stream aggregates, nightly exact recompute, HyperLogLog for uniques) and the abuse controls (reputation scanning off the create path, open-redirect validation, rate limits, takedown), and explain what breaks at 10× and 100×.
Estimate the monthly cost and name the lines that scale with clicks rather than links, and sketch the multi-region evolution.
